No, the conviction should not be reversed on causation: the defective drug was a but-for cause of the earlier death, and a defendant who hastens a death is not excused because the victim was already terminally ill. The team note is wrong that murder requires intent to kill, since common-law and Model Penal Code murder also reach killings committed with extreme indifference to human life, and knowingly shipping a known sub-strength cancer drug to patients who depend on it can meet that standard, though a business motive alone would not. Reversal would be warranted only if the jury was instructed that intent to kill was required, or if the evidence did not show he knew the lot posed a risk to patients' lives.

CONFIDENCE: 62
